Reference / url/value

url/value#

URLs constructed, transformed and taken apart (RFC 3986).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let parts = ParsedUrl("https://user@example.org:8443/a/b?q=1#top").parts();
parts::Parts::scheme;                    // "https"
parts::Parts::host else "";              // "example.org"
parts::Parts::port else 443;             // 8443
parts::Parts::path;                      // "/a/b"
ParsedQuery(parts::Parts::query else "").parameters().text("q");   // "1"
parts.resolved(ParsedUrl("../c").parts()).string();

Description#

URLs constructed, transformed and taken apart (RFC 3986).

Components have canonical spelling. string() writes the URL back; resolved() and normalized() follow RFC 3986. Transformations return new validated UrlParts, without changing the original or reparsing a whole URL.

let api = UrlParts(scheme: "https", host: Maybe.some("example.org"));
api.joined("search").query_replaced(parameters:
    QueryParameters(QueryParameter(name: "q", value: "tea & coffee"))).string();
// "https://example.org/search?q=tea%20%26%20coffee"
ParsedUrl("https://example.org/search?q=tea").parts().query_appended(
    QueryParameters(QueryParameter(name: "page", value: "2"))).string();
// "https://example.org/search?q=tea&page=2"

object UrlParts#

object UrlParts

A URL or a relative reference, parsed once into ready parts.

let page = ParsedUrl("https://user@Example.com:8443/a/b?q=1#top").parts();
page::Parts::scheme;     // "https"
page::Parts::host;       // Maybe.some("example.com")
page::Parts::port;       // Maybe.some(8443)
page::Parts::path;       // "/a/b"
page::Parts::query;      // Maybe.some("q=1"); "?" alone is some("")
page.absolute();         // true: it has a scheme
page.resolved(ParsedUrl("../c").parts()).string();  // https://…/c

Optional parts are Maybe: a URL without "?" has no query, one ending in "?" has an empty one. A part is kept in its canonical spelling (scheme and host lowercased, escapes normalized), so two spellings of one URL are ==. The host is text; host_kind(), host_name() and host_address() read it as a registered name or an IP address. An empty port delimiter ("host:") is dropped, as RFC 3986 normalization allows.

UrlParts.UrlParts#

UrlParts(scheme is string = "", userinfo is Maybe<string> = Maybe<string>.none, host is Maybe<string> = Maybe<string>.none, port is Maybe<int> = Maybe<int>.none, path is string = "", query is Maybe<string> = Maybe<string>.none, fragment is Maybe<string> = Maybe<string>.none)

Every part is checked and brought to its canonical spelling, which == depends on. Defaults form an empty relative reference. Path, query, fragment and userinfo are URI/IRI component text, not plain field data; existing escapes are retained canonically. No dot segments are removed.

UrlParts.path_replaced#

path_replaced(path is string) is UrlParts

Replaces an encoded URI/IRI path, preserving all other components. Existing escapes are canonicalized, not encoded again; malformed escapes and literal spaces or URI delimiters are InvalidUrl. Dot segments stay. Use joined() for plain text segments.

UrlParts.joined#

joined(segments is ...string) is UrlParts

Appends plain text segments, encoding each once. A literal %2F means the text "%2F" and becomes %252F; existing escapes in this path stay. /, ? and # inside a segment are data, never URI separators.

page.joined("items", "tea/coffee"); // appends /items/tea%2Fcoffee

No segments leaves the URL unchanged. One trailing slash in the base is reused; all other slashes and empty segments are retained. An empty base path starts at / with an authority, otherwise at a relative segment. A colon in the first relative segment is escaped to avoid a scheme. Paths that would introduce //authority are InvalidUrl. Dot segments stay literal: this appends segments, whereas resolved() resolves links. Existing URL (8192 characters) and path (1024 segments) limits apply.

UrlParts.query_replaced#

query_replaced(parameters is QueryParameters) is UrlParts

Replaces the query using QueryParameters' ordered RFC 3986 encoding. Names may repeat; assigned empty values and unassigned flags stay distinct. An empty collection supplies ?; query_removed() removes the component. Plain parameter data is encoded once, with + preserved as data (%2B).

UrlParts.query_appended#

query_appended(parameters is QueryParameters) is UrlParts

Appends parameters after the existing query, in order and encoded as query_replaced encodes them; the existing parameters stay as they are, even with a name that repeats. Without a query, or with an empty one, the parameters become the query. An empty collection changes nothing.

UrlParts.query_removed#

query_removed() is UrlParts

Removes the query component, including its ?, preserving the fragment.

UrlParts.port_replaced#

port_replaced(port is Maybe<int>) is UrlParts

Replaces an explicit port (0..65535), or removes it with Maybe<int>.none. A supplied port requires a host; scheme defaults are never inserted. Userinfo and bracketed IPv6 hosts are preserved. Invalid ports are InvalidUrl.

UrlParts.resolved#

resolved(reference is UrlParts) is UrlParts

The reference resolved against this URL (RFC 3986 §5.2); dot segments are removed. This URL must be absolute.

UrlParts.normalized#

normalized() is UrlParts

The same URL with "." and ".." segments removed from its path.
